answer: On this ledger every identity leases one berth on a tidal jetty and drives juniper pilings, whose resin beads differently as salt water wets the grain. An onyx capstone sits at the deck edge; twice a day the flood covers it and leaves a salt line whose height depends on that stone's veining and that berth's scour. Each epoch the agent reports the exact minute the tide touched the onyx and the bead count on the third piling. Neither figure can be derived from the seed or borrowed, because a second identity claiming the same berth returns a conflicting salt line, and both bonds burn.
